newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Jul/Aug gas oil spread widens.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Jul/Aug gas oil spread widens.

text.p: Singapore front month gas oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Tuesday but the August paper is firming on expectations of improved demand in the further out months leading to a widening to the contango, traders said.
"The July/August spread is widening because people think demand will pick up later in the third quarter," one trader said.

July paper was last quoted steady from late Monday at $22.45/$22.55 per barrel, brokers said. The market traded earlier in the day at $22.50, down sharply from Monday's intra-day traded high of $23.05.
Most of the trading activity for the day centred around August where there is a growing belief that prices will pick up as fresh demand kicks in.
August traded earlier in the day from a low of $22.83 to $22.95 with several hundred thousand barrels exchanging hands, brokers said. August was last quoted at $22.90/$23.00.

As a result the July/August time spread has widened to last quote at minus 55 to minus 40 cents. It traded this morning at minus 35 cents, compared to late last week's minus 25 cents traded level, brokers said.

Traders said the firmer August prices were due to market perceptions that current prompt overhang would have cleared by then and prices will pick up as the big buyers such as China, India and Indonesia return to the market.

India issued two term tenders to purchase 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 percent sulphur diesel for August 1997 to March 1998 delivery, on top of the 3.2 million tonnes it had already bought on a one-year term basis for June 1997 to May 1998 delivery.
Indonesian July and August purchases are expected to increase due to shutdown of crude units at Balikpapan and Cilacap for maintenance.
Chinese buying was also anticipated because China had cut back its second quarter demand considerably due to high purchases of just over 2 million tonnes in the first quarter.
Also low physical prices in Singapore might encourage some buyers to come out and bargain pick, traders said.
On Monday, a 150,000 barrel cargo for July 1-5 lifting traded at $22.20 per barrel free-on-board Singapore-- the lowest level in 18 months.
Fuel oil swaps were steady with July last quoted at $100.00/$101.00, brokers said.
Naphtha swaps were down due to poor demand in Japan with July last quoted at $20.80/$21.10, down from Monday's $21.10/$21.30, brokers said.
They said July traded late Monday at $20.975 while August traded at $21.20.
